name: __v4l2_async_register_subdev
prose: Precondition: sd points to a valid v4l2_subdev and the caller does not hold list_lock. Postcondition: it reinitialises sd->asc_list. If sd->fwnode is NULL and sd->dev is set it sets sd->fwnode to dev_fwnode(sd->dev); otherwise, if fwnode_graph_is_endpoint(sd->fwnode) is true, it warns and returns -EINVAL, before taking list_lock and without touching sd->owner. Otherwise it sets sd->owner to module and takes list_lock. For each notifier on the global notifier list that has a v4l2_device, it loops while v4l2_async_find_match finds a matching connection asc for sd: it calls v4l2_async_match_notify (a non-zero result goes to the exit that releases list_lock, sets sd->owner to NULL and returns that error, with nothing unbound), then v4l2_async_nf_try_subdev_notifier (a non-zero result unbinds that one connection asc, then releases the lock, sets sd->owner to NULL and returns the error), then v4l2_async_nf_try_complete (a non-zero result first unbinds all sub-devices of sd's own subdev notifier, if it has one, and then also unbinds asc as in the previous case, releases the lock, sets sd->owner to NULL and returns the error). When the loops finish without error it adds sd to subdev_list (whether or not any connection matched), releases list_lock and returns 0 with sd->owner set to module. A fwnode that was taken from sd->dev stays set on the failure paths.
note: Reviewer 1 right (the -EINVAL endpoint return is before sd->owner is set); reviewer 2 right (match_notify failure only unlocks and clears owner; try_subdev_notifier failure unbinds one connection; success always adds sd to subdev_list, v4l2-async.c:855-860); reviewer 3 right (try_complete failure unbinds all subdevs of sd's subdev notifier and falls through to the single-connection unbind, 862-872; and sd->fwnode may be set from sd->dev at 821-822). __v4l2_async_register_subdev at 804-880.

name: handler_new_ref
prose: Precondition: hdl is a valid initialised v4l2_ctrl_handler (nr_of_buckets, ctrl_refs, buckets and lock set up) and ctrl is a valid control; ctrl_ref may be NULL. A control with the same id may already be registered, it is not an error. Postcondition: this is handler_new_ref. If ctrl_ref is non-NULL, *ctrl_ref is first set to NULL. If the control is not a compound type, is not the class control of its class and the handler has no class control yet, it creates the class control with v4l2_ctrl_new_std and returns hdl->error if that fails. It then returns hdl->error if the handler already has an error. It allocates the v4l2_ctrl_ref with kzalloc (extra space for a request value if allocate_req is set and the control is not an array) and on failure returns the result of handler_set_err(hdl, -ENOMEM), i.e. the handler error is set to -ENOMEM. With hdl->lock held it inserts the new ref into the id-sorted ctrl_refs list (at the end if the list is empty or the id is above the last, otherwise before the first ref with a greater id); if a ref with the same id is already in the list it frees the new ref and goes to the unlock exit, so nothing is inserted, *ctrl_ref stays NULL and the function still returns 0. Otherwise it links the ref at the head of the hash bucket (id % nr_of_buckets), sets *ctrl_ref to it if ctrl_ref is non-NULL and, if ctrl->handler is hdl, sets ctrl->cluster to the ref's ctrl pointer and ctrl->ncontrols to 1. It releases hdl->lock and returns 0.
note: Not a drop: the slice 1837-2092 starts inside handler_new_ref (v4l2-ctrls-core.c:1813-1894), which is a real function. The old prose's precondition 'the control id is not already registered' was wrong: a duplicate id frees the new ref and returns 0 (1869-1872); it also omitted the class-control creation, the error returns and the unset *ctrl_ref. I read the whole function.

name: try_or_set_cluster
prose: Precondition: the lock of master's handler is held, master->cluster and master->ncontrols are initialised, and each control whose new value the caller supplied has is_new set. Postcondition: it walks the cluster in index order (skipping NULL entries). For a control without is_new it copies the current value to the new value (cur_to_new); for a control with is_new, if set is true and the control has V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_GRABBED, it returns -EBUSY immediately, so controls after that index have not been processed by this loop (those before it already had cur_to_new applied), and no control op has been called. Otherwise it calls the master's try_ctrl op (call_op gives 0 if the op is absent) and returns its result if non-zero. If set is false, or cluster_changed reports no change, it returns the try_ctrl result (0 here) without calling s_ctrl or new_to_cur. Otherwise it calls the master's s_ctrl op and returns its result if non-zero (the new values are then not made current). On success it records whether the manual/auto state differs between the current and new values; when the new state is manual, differs from the current state, the cluster has volatile controls, it marks each non-master control present in the cluster as changed; it then calls new_to_cur on every index of the cluster (NULL entries are handled by new_to_cur) with ch_flags, plus V4L2_EVENT_CTRL_CH_FLAGS for non-master controls when the mode flipped, and returns 0. The function takes and releases no locks itself.
note: Reviewer 2 right (cur_to_new is applied to non-is_new controls even when set is false; the old prose said the first loop copied for every control before the GRABBED check); reviewer 3 right (the -EBUSY return in the middle of the loop skips the controls after it, v4l2-ctrls-core.c:2550-2566, so it is not 'every' control); reviewer 1 right (new_to_cur only when set and cluster changed). try_or_set_cluster at 2537-2596.

name: v4l2_flash_s_ctrl
prose: Precondition: c is a control of the v4l2_flash control handler, so v4l2_ctrl_to_v4l2_flash(c) yields a v4l2_flash whose ctrls array was filled in by v4l2_flash_init_controls; fled_cdev may be NULL. Postcondition: for V4L2_CID_FLASH_TORCH_INTENSITY and V4L2_CID_FLASH_INDICATOR_INTENSITY it returns the result of v4l2_flash_set_led_brightness, whether or not fled_cdev exists. For any other control it returns -EINVAL if fled_cdev is NULL. Otherwise: for V4L2_CID_FLASH_LED_MODE, mode NONE turns the LED off with led_set_brightness_sync and returns the result of led_set_flash_strobe(false); mode FLASH turns the torch LED off and, only if a STROBE_SOURCE control exists, returns the result of the external_strobe_set flash op for the chosen strobe source (call_flash_op yields -EINVAL if the driver has no such op), returning 0 if there is no STROBE_SOURCE control; mode TORCH, if a STROBE_SOURCE control exists, first calls external_strobe_set(false) and returns a negative result, then calls led_set_flash_strobe(false) and returns a negative result, and finally returns the result of v4l2_flash_set_led_brightness for the TORCH_INTENSITY control; any other LED mode value falls through to -EINVAL. For V4L2_CID_FLASH_STROBE_SOURCE it returns 0 without touching the hardware if the LED mode control is not FLASH (the setting is only cached), otherwise the result of the external_strobe_set op. For V4L2_CID_FLASH_STROBE and V4L2_CID_FLASH_STROBE_STOP it returns -EBUSY when the software strobe mode is inactive, otherwise the result of led_set_flash_strobe(true or false). For V4L2_CID_FLASH_TIMEOUT it returns led_set_flash_timeout and for V4L2_CID_FLASH_INTENSITY led_set_flash_brightness. Any other control id returns -EINVAL. The helpers' results may be negative errors, and the LED-off calls ahead of some returns are not checked. No locks or references are taken in this function.
note: Reviewer 1 right (helper errors are returned), reviewer 2 right (LED_MODE and INDICATOR_INTENSITY paths were missing), reviewer 3 right (the TORCH path ends with v4l2_flash_set_led_brightness, not call_flash_op, v4l2-flash-led-class.c:251-265; the flash op is called only when a STROBE_SOURCE control exists). Also: TORCH/INDICATOR intensity are handled before the fled_cdev NULL test (222-226). Extra: call_flash_op returns -EINVAL if the op is missing (line 20-23). v4l2_flash_s_ctrl at 213-304.

name: v4l_print_streamparm
prose: Precondition: arg points to a readable struct v4l2_streamparm; write_only is not used. Postcondition: this is v4l_print_streamparm. It continues the current kernel log line with pr_cont: it prints the buffer type name and then, if p->type is V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE or VIDEO_CAPTURE_MPLANE, the capture parameters (capability, capturemode, timeperframe numerator/denominator, extendedmode, readbuffers) and a newline; or, if p->type is V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_OUTPUT or VIDEO_OUTPUT_MPLANE, the output parameters (capability, outputmode, timeperframe, extendedmode, writebuffers) and a newline; for any other type it prints only a newline. It returns nothing, modifies nothing and takes no locks.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is v4l_print_streamparm (v4l2-ioctl.c:501-526); there is no v4l_print_parm. The old prose matched the behaviour. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: v4l2_jpeg_decode_subsampling
prose: Precondition: nf and h_v are u8 values (0..255); no other constraint. Postcondition: if nf == 1 it returns V4L2_JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING_GRAY (5) whatever h_v is; otherwise, if nf == 4 and h_v != 0x11, it returns -EINVAL (-22); otherwise it returns V4L2_JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING_444 (0) for h_v == 0x11, 422 (1) for 0x21, 420 (2) for 0x22, 411 (3) for 0x41, and -EINVAL (-22) for any other h_v. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Old prose and contract said GRAY is 4; in uapi v4l2-controls.h:1198-1203 the enumerators are 444=0, 422=1, 420=2, 411=3, 410=4 and GRAY=5, so the GRAY return is 5. Everything else matches v4l2-jpeg.c:248-269. Mechanical reviewer complaints concerned older contracts only.

name: check_which
prose: Precondition: none; which may be any u32. Postcondition: it returns 0 when which is V4L2_SUBDEV_FORMAT_TRY (0) or V4L2_SUBDEV_FORMAT_ACTIVE (1), and -EINVAL (-22) for every other value. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires 	rue; ensures ((which == 0 || which == 1) ==> result == 0) && ((which != 0 && which != 1) ==> result == -22); */
note: Matches v4l2-subdev.c:190-197 (static inline). The repeated 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical complaints about earlier contracts. Contract rewritten as two implications; value of the enumerators TRY=0 and ACTIVE=1 checked in v4l2-subdev.h (uapi).

name: v4l2_subdev_enable_streams
prose: Precondition: sd is a valid initialised subdev whose media entity has valid pads and a media device, pad is a pad index and streams_mask is a 64-bit stream bitmask. Postcondition: in this order it returns -EINVAL if pad >= sd->entity.num_pads; -EOPNOTSUPP if the pad is not a source pad; -EOPNOTSUPP if pad is 64 or more (the enabled_pads bitmask is 64 bits); and 0 with no further effect if streams_mask is 0 (so a zero mask on a bad pad still returns an error). If the subdev has a pad enable_streams op it takes the active state lock (v4l2_subdev_lock_and_get_active_state) and later unlocks it; otherwise it falls back to the s_stream op with no state (NULL), where streams are tracked in sd->enabled_pads. It collects the existing and the enabled streams of the pad; if not all requested streams exist it returns -EINVAL, and if any requested stream is already enabled it returns -EALREADY (the state lock is released on these returns). It then either calls the pad enable_streams op with the state, pad and mask, or, in the fallback, calls .s_stream(sd, 1) only if the subdev is not already streaming (otherwise treating the result as 0). If the call returns non-zero it returns that error with no stream marked enabled. On success it marks the requested streams enabled (in the active state, or in sd->enabled_pads in the fallback) and, only when the enable_streams op was used and the subdev was not already streaming, enables the privacy LED. It returns 0 on success and does not hold the state lock after returning.
note: Reviewer 1 right (the source-pad -EOPNOTSUPP check, v4l2-subdev.c:2324-2325; and old prose put the zero-mask return first: it comes after the pad checks, 2334-2335); reviewer 2 right (the fallback calls .s_stream(1) only when not already streaming, 2375-2378); reviewer 3 right (in the fallback state is NULL and the enabled streams are tracked in sd->enabled_pads, 2338-2343). v4l2_subdev_enable_streams at 2306-2405. I did not read v4l2_subdev_set_streams_enabled or collect_streams bodies.

name: merge_prob
prose: Precondition: ct0 + ct1 and ct0 * 256 + (ct0 + ct1) / 2 fit in an unsigned 32-bit integer (the arithmetic wraps otherwise); count_sat is between 1 and 256 (fastdiv has a reciprocal table only for divisors 2 to 256: a divisor of 0 gives a factor of 0, 1 returns the dividend, and a divisor of 257 or more triggers WARN_ON and returns the dividend unchanged); max_update_factor is at most 256. Postcondition: it returns pre_prob unchanged when ct0 + ct1 is zero. Otherwise, with den = ct0 + ct1, prob = ((ct0 * 256 + den / 2) / den) clamped to [1, 255], count = min(den, count_sat) and factor = max_update_factor * count / count_sat (computed by fastdiv, exact for the allowed ranges), it returns pre_prob + (((prob - pre_prob) * factor + 128) >> 8) in u32 arithmetic truncated to u8, which for the allowed ranges equals (pre_prob * (256 - factor) + prob * factor + 128) / 256 (integer division) and lies in [0, 255] (it is between pre_prob and prob). It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires 1 <= count_sat <= 256; requires max_update_factor <= 256; requires ct0 + ct1 <= 4294967295; requires ct0 * 256 + (ct0 + ct1) / 2 <= 4294967295; ensures 0 <= result && result <= 255; ensures (ct0 + ct1 == 0) ==> result == pre_prob; */
note: The old prose required only count_sat nonzero, but factor comes from fastdiv (v4l2-vp9.c:1107-1155), whose reciprocal table covers divisors 2..256 only; larger divisors hit WARN_ON and return the dividend. The result formula was right (the u32 wrap of prob - pre_prob cancels modulo 256 after the u8 truncation, and the shifted sum equals the floor expression). The reviewer's complaint that the contract omitted the 'nonzero-sum adjustment' is mechanical; I trimmed the contract to the bounds and the zero-sum case, which I can state exactly, rather than the long closed form. merge_prob at 1483-1507.

name: gpmc_round_ps_to_sync_clk
prose: Precondition: the GPMC functional clock period (gpmc_get_fclk_period) is non-zero; sync_clk is such that gpmc_calc_divider(sync_clk) returns a divider in 1..4 (that function returns 1 for a tick count of 0 or 1, the tick count up to 4, and -1 if the tick count is above 4; a divider of -1 makes the rounding meaningless); and time_ps and the intermediate tick counts are small enough that the 32-bit additions, the product of the rounded tick count with div and the final tick-to-picosecond conversion do not wrap. Postcondition: it computes div = gpmc_calc_divider(sync_clk), converts time_ps to fclk ticks rounding up (gpmc_ps_to_ticks), rounds that tick count up to a multiple of div, and returns that many ticks converted back to picoseconds (ticks * fclk period). Both steps round up, so the result is the smallest multiple of div fclk periods that is not less than time_ps, and it is 0 exactly when time_ps is 0. It depends on the current fclk period (global clock state), takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer 4 wrong: gpmc_ps_to_ticks rounds UP, (time_ps + tick_ps - 1) / tick_ps (omap-gpmc.c:351-359), so the result is not below time_ps. Reviewer 2 right (the divider must be positive: gpmc_calc_divider returns -1 for sync_clk above four ticks, 681-691; the old prose said -EINVAL); reviewer 1 right (overflow bound needed). Contract left empty: the function reads the global fclk period. gpmc_round_ps_to_sync_clk at 1530-1539.

name: SET_LAN_PACKET_LENGTH
note: Not a function: SET_LAN_PACKET_LENGTH (mpi_lan.h:170-173) is a function-like macro, not a C function (defined at the cited header line). Semantics for the record: it assigns to its first argument, keeping all bits outside the field mask and replacing the field with ((value << shift) & mask); field = bits 0..15 (mask 0x0000FFFF, shift 0). Out-of-range values are masked off rather than being a precondition violation, and the first argument is evaluated more than once (it must be an lvalue without side effects). Previous 'dropped' decision correct.

name: mpt_do_ioc_recovery
prose: Precondition: ioc is a valid initialised MPT_ADAPTER with mapped chip and pcidev; ioc->alt_ioc is NULL or a valid sibling adapter; reason is MPT_HOSTEVENT_IOC_BRINGUP or MPT_HOSTEVENT_IOC_RECOVER; sleepFlag says whether the helpers may sleep. Postcondition: it masks the reply interrupts and clears ioc->active, and does the same for the alt IOC if that is active or reason is RECOVER (remembering that in reset_alt_ioc_active). It calls MakeIocReady (hard reset unless BRINGUP): on failure it returns -1 (after, for a result of -4 'owned by peer', re-enabling the alt IOC's interrupts and active flag if it had been disabled). It may bring the alt IOC ready (MakeIocReady on it after a hard reset), calls GetIocFacts up to 5 times (if all fail ret is -2, but the rest of the function still runs the alt-IOC parts and the steps guarded by ret == 0 are skipped), and gets the alt IOC's facts, clearing alt_ioc_ready and reset_alt_ioc_active if that fails twice. Only if ret is still 0 and reason is BRINGUP with the firmware-download-boot flag set it re-enables the PCI device and regions, returning -5 directly (not through the cleanup at the out label) if pci_enable_device or pci_request_selected_regions fails. For BRINGUP with ret 0 it enables MSI if configured and requests the shared IRQ; a request_irq failure disables MSI again and returns -EBUSY via out. Then, while ret is 0, PrimeIocFifos (failure sets ret -3) and SendIocInit (failure sets ret -4) run; the alt IOC gets the same two steps if it is ready, a failure there only clearing alt_ioc_ready and reset_alt_ioc_active. For BRINGUP with ioc->upload_fw and ret 0 it calls mpt_do_upload (failure sets ret -6). If ret is 0 and no event state is set it calls SendEventNotification and takes its result as ret; the alt IOC's SendEventNotification result is stored in rc. If ret is 0 it unmasks the reply interrupt and sets ioc->active to 1. If rc is 0 (rc holds the result of the last helper whose value was stored in it, so a non-zero value left by a failed main-IOC or alt-IOC step also suppresses this) and reset_alt_ioc_active is set, it re-enables the alt IOC's interrupt and active flag. For BRINGUP with ret still 0 it initialises the inactive RAID volume list and runs bus-type-specific setup (for SAS it may clear the persistence table with mptbase_sas_persist_operation, whose non-zero result becomes ret and exits through out), then GetIoUnitPage2 and mpt_get_manufacturing_pg_0. At out, if ret is non-zero and the IRQ was allocated here, it frees the IRQ and disables MSI if enabled. It returns ret: 0 on success or one of -1 to -4, -5, -6, -EBUSY, or the error from SendEventNotification or mptbase_sas_persist_operation.
note: Reviewer 4 right: a failure of the alt IOC's SendEventNotification does not clear alt_ioc_ready/reset_alt_ioc_active and does not change the return value (mptbase.c:2513-2514), but it does leave rc non-zero, which only suppresses the alt re-enable at 2521; so the old statement 'alt-IOC failures only clear the flags and never change the return value' was incomplete. Also: -2 does not end the function (it continues to the alt-IOC steps), and the -5 return bypasses the out label (2394-2398). mpt_do_ioc_recovery at 2285-2619 read fully.

name: GetIocFacts
prose: Precondition: ioc points to a valid MPT_ADAPTER structure, sleepFlag says whether the caller may sleep, and reason is the host-event code (MPT_HOSTEVENT_IOC_BRINGUP or another); the function builds its IOCFacts request on the stack and uses ioc->facts as the reply buffer, so the caller supplies and keeps only ioc. Postcondition: if ioc->last_state is MPI_IOC_STATE_RESET the function returns -44 without modifying the adapter; otherwise it zeroes ioc->facts and sends the request with mpt_handshake_req_reply_wait, returning that call's nonzero result unchanged on failure; if the reply MsgLength is not greater than offsetof(IOCFactsReply_t, RequestFrameSize)/sizeof(u32) it prints an error and returns -66; otherwise it byte-swaps the reply fields, saves ioc->FirstWhoInit from facts->WhoInit when reason is MPT_HOSTEVENT_IOC_BRINGUP and FirstWhoInit was WHOINIT_UNKNOWN, sets ioc->ir_firmware to 1 when the ProductID product field exceeds MPI_FW_HEADER_PID_PROD_TARGET_SCSI, aligns facts->FWImageSize, returns -55 if facts->RequestFrameSize is zero, sets ioc->NB_for_64_byte_frame (computed as ((63 / (BlockSize * 4)) + 1) & 3, which divides by zero if the device reports a BlockSize of 0, as there is no check) and ioc->NBShiftFactor from facts->BlockSize, and when reason is MPT_HOSTEVENT_IOC_BRINGUP also sets ioc->req_sz, ioc->req_depth, ioc->reply_sz and ioc->reply_depth and calls GetPortFacts(ioc, 0, sleepFlag), returning its nonzero result unchanged; it returns 0 on success, and on the -55, -66 and handshake error paths ioc->facts may be left zeroed or only partially byte-swapped and the other ioc fields listed above may be left unset or stale.
note: Reviewer 4 wrong: the reset-state path returns -44 (mptbase.c:3083), not -4. The rest of the old prose matches GetIocFacts at 3066-3229; I added the unchecked division by BlockSize (3189). Slice cut the head. Read fully.

name: mpt_diag_reset
prose: Precondition: ioc points to a valid, initialised MPT_ADAPTER whose chip registers are mapped; sleepFlag is CAN_SLEEP or NO_SLEEP; ignore is non-zero to force a reset regardless of the reset-history bit. Postcondition: it first clears IntStatus. For a SAS1078 (device id MPI_MANUFACTPAGE_DEVID_SAS1078) with ignore zero it returns 0 and does nothing else; with ignore non-zero it writes the 1078 reset register, calls the registered protocol reset handlers with MPT_IOC_PRE_RESET, then polls the doorbell once per second up to 60 times and returns 1 as soon as the IOC state is READY, or -1 if it never is (these SAS1078 paths return without the diagnostic-register steps and without clearing facts.EventState). For other devices it reads the Diagnostic register; if ignore is non-zero or the reset-history bit is clear it enables diagnostic mode with the magic write sequence (returning -2 if DRWE is still not set after more than 20 attempts), disables the ARM, hits the reset bit and sets hard_reset_done, calls the reset handlers (also for the alt IOC) and then waits for the reload: with cached firmware (own or alt IOC's) it polls the diagnostic reset bit for up to 30 seconds and calls mpt_downloadboot, whose failure is only logged; otherwise it polls the doorbell for READY for up to 60 seconds and only logs if READY is not reached. In both cases it then clears the reset-history bit: it re-enables diagnostic mode with the magic sequence (a failure after more than 20 attempts only logs and exits that loop, it does not return), clears MPI_DIAG_RESET_HISTORY, logs if the bit does not clear, and closes diagnostic mode. It re-reads the Diagnostic register and returns -3 if any of MPI_DIAG_FLASH_BAD_SIG, MPI_DIAG_RESET_ADAPTER or MPI_DIAG_DISABLE_ARM is set (this check applies whether or not a reset was performed). Otherwise it sets ioc->facts.EventState (and the alt IOC's) to 0 and returns 1 if a diagnostic reset was performed, or 0 if it was not (ignore zero and reset-history bit set). It takes no locks.
note: Reviewer 1 right (0 for a non-SAS1078 with ignore zero and the history bit set; the old prose had it); reviewer 2 right (-2 after 21 attempts, 'more than 20', mptbase.c:4048-4052); reviewer 3 wrong: the final check at 4219-4223 tests FLASH_BAD_SIG, RESET_ADAPTER and DISABLE_ARM together, so -3 is not limited to the cached-firmware path. I added the unmentioned effects: the SAS1078 paths skip the diagnostic steps, the history-clear loop does not return -2, the reset handlers are called, and facts.EventState is cleared at the end. mpt_diag_reset at 3954-4242.

name: PrimeIocFifos
prose: Precondition: ioc points to a valid MPT_ADAPTER whose chip registers are mapped and whose reply_sz, reply_depth, req_sz, req_depth, pcidev and dma_mask are valid; its pools may already be allocated (ioc->reply_frames non-NULL) or not. Postcondition: if ioc->reply_frames is already non-NULL it skips all allocation and only writes ioc->reply_depth reply-frame DMA addresses (starting at ioc->alloc_dma, ioc->reply_sz apart) to the IOC ReplyFifo and returns 0, touching no list, lock or DMA mask. Otherwise it first calls initChainBuffers (a negative result returns -1 at once). For a SAS1078 with ioc->dma_mask above 35 bits it sets 32-bit DMA and coherent masks as a workaround; if that fails it restores 64-bit masks and returns -1. It allocates one coherent buffer for the reply frames, request frames and chain buffers (on failure it goes to out_fail), zeroes it, records it in ioc->alloc, alloc_dma, alloc_sz, reply_frames, req_frames, ChainBuffer and the low-DMA fields and adds its size to ioc->alloc_total, builds ioc->FreeChainQ from the chain buffers and ioc->FreeQ from the req_depth request frames (the latter under ioc->FreeQlock with spin_lock_irqsave), then allocates the coherent sense-buffer pool (on failure goes to out_fail) and adds its size to ioc->alloc_total. It then writes the reply-frame addresses to the ReplyFifo, restores ioc->dma_mask as the DMA and coherent mask if the 35-bit workaround had been applied, and returns 0. At out_fail, if ioc->alloc is non-NULL it frees it, sets ioc->reply_frames and ioc->req_frames to NULL (ioc->alloc itself is not cleared) and subtracts its size from ioc->alloc_total; if ioc->sense_buf_pool is non-NULL it frees it and sets it to NULL without adjusting ioc->alloc_total; if the workaround had been applied it restores 64-bit DMA masks; it returns -1.
note: Reviewer 3 right: out_fail frees the sense buffer pool but only subtracts the main allocation from alloc_total (mptbase.c:4602-4615), while the old prose said it subtracts the freed sizes (plural). Reviewers 1 and 2 right and already covered (the already-allocated path does not repopulate queues, take locks or touch DMA masks since dma_mask stays 0). Extra: ioc->alloc is not NULLed after the free. PrimeIocFifos at 4423-4624.

name: arizona_irq_init
prose: Precondition: arizona is a valid arizona device with regmap, dev, irq and pdata set, and arizona->type is one of the chip types compiled in (WM5102, WM5110/WM8280, WM1831/CS47L24, WM8997, WM8998/WM1814 under their config options). Postcondition: it sets arizona->ctrlif_error to true and then to false for every supported type, so for those types the control-interface-error IRQ is never requested; an unlisted type returns -EINVAL (the preceding BUG_ON condition is never true). It selects the AOD IRQ chip (NULL for CS47L24/WM1831) and the main IRQ chip, writes 0 to ARIZONA_WAKE_CONTROL (the result is ignored), and, if pdata.irq_flags is 0, reads the trigger type from the IRQ descriptor, returning -EINVAL if there is no irq_data, and defaulting to IRQF_TRIGGER_LOW for no or an unsupported trigger type. For a high or rising trigger it clears the IRQ polarity bit (an error goes to the exit with that error, nothing yet to undo). It creates a two-entry virtual IRQ domain (NULL result returns -EINVAL), maps the AOD index and adds the AOD regmap IRQ chip if there is one, maps the main index and adds the main regmap IRQ chip; a mapping failure returns -EINVAL and a regmap_add_irq_chip failure returns its error, in each case after undoing what was set up before (IRQ chips, mappings and the domain). With CONFIG_GPIOLIB_LEGACY and pdata.irq_gpio set it may replace arizona->irq by gpio_to_irq(pdata.irq_gpio) with a warning, and a failed devm_gpio_request_one is only logged and clears pdata.irq_gpio. It requests the threaded primary IRQ and then the boot-done IRQ; a failure of either returns its error after freeing the earlier IRQ requests and undoing the chips, mappings and domain. If ctrlif_error is true (not the case for the listed types) it requests the control-interface-error IRQ with the same unwind on failure. On success it returns 0.
note: Reviewer right: irq_domain_create_linear failure returns -EINVAL (arizona-irq.c:315-319); old prose omitted it as a distinct case. Extra finding: every supported chip case sets arizona->ctrlif_error = false (lines 222, 239, 248, 256, 265), so the CTRLIF_ERR request at 394-404 is not reached for the listed types. arizona_irq_init at 206-430.

name: cs47l15_16bit_readable_register
prose: Precondition: dev is unused and may be anything; reg is any unsigned int value. Postcondition: this is cs47l15_16bit_readable_register, the regmap readable-register callback for the CS47L15's 16-bit register map. It returns true exactly when reg equals one of the register constants or lies within one of the inclusive GNU case ranges listed in its switch (about 460 case labels, including the software reset and hardware revision registers, write-sequencer, tone generator, PWM drive, sample-rate and always-on sequence selectors, haptics, mixer input source and volume, FX, EQ, DRC, HPLPF, ISRC, GPIO, IRQ status/mask/raw-status registers, the interrupt debounce register and IRQ1_CTRL), and false for every other value (default case). It performs no I/O, reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: the function is cs47l15_16bit_readable_register(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg) (cs47l15-tables.c:712-1181), not madera_readable_reg. I counted 461 case labels and the two returns (true for the labels, false for default) but did not compare each label with the datasheet. Mechanical reviewer right on the name. Contract left empty: the register list is too long to state faithfully in one line.

name: madera_dev_init
prose: Precondition: madera points to a valid struct madera whose dev, regmap, regmap_32bit, type, type_name and pdata fields are set (the function itself acquires the mclk clocks and the reset GPIO); the caller keeps nothing held. Postcondition: this is madera_dev_init. It sets drvdata, initialises the notifier and mutex, copies the platform data if any, gets the three mclk clocks with devm_clk_bulk_get_optional and the reset GPIO with madera_get_reset_gpio (a failure of either returns its error at once, with no unwinding), and puts both regmaps in cache-only mode. By madera->type it sets reset_errata for CS47L15, does nothing for the CS47L35/90/91/92/93 types, adds the LDO1 child devices with mfd_add_devices for CS47L85 and WM1840 (a failure returns that error at once, mfd_add_devices having removed what it added itself), and returns -ENODEV for any other type, again with no unwinding. It then gets the core supplies (devm_regulator_bulk_get) and DCVDD (regulator_get, not devm), enables the core supplies and DCVDD, releases the hard reset (before or after DCVDD depending on reset_errata), takes both regmaps out of cache-only, waits for boot (madera_wait_for_boot_noack), reads the silicon ID from MADERA_SOFTWARE_RESET and selects the patch function and mfd cell list from the ID and the type: an unknown ID returns -EINVAL and a known ID that does not match madera->type (or whose config option is off) returns -ENODEV. It soft-resets if there is no hard reset or the reset errata applies, waits for boot, reads and masks madera->rev, applies the patch, enables MCLK2 with clk_prepare_enable and writes MADERA_CLOCK_32K_1 to select it, sets runtime PM active and enabled with a 100 ms autosuspend delay, and adds the subdevices with mfd_add_devices; every failing step returns its error after unwinding in reverse order: pm_runtime_disable if runtime PM was enabled, clk_disable_unprepare of MCLK2 after its enable succeeded, re-asserting the hard reset and regulator_disable of DCVDD (not done if the DCVDD enable itself failed), regulator_bulk_disable of the core supplies (not done if their enable failed), regulator_put of DCVDD (the pointer is not cleared) and mfd_remove_devices. On success it returns 0 with DCVDD, the core supplies and MCLK2 enabled (the caller must later disable and release them), runtime PM enabled and the child devices registered.
note: Reviewer right on the LDO1 failure: mfd_add_devices failure for CS47L85/WM1840 returns directly (madera-core.c:527-530) without the mfd_remove_devices unwind, and the unknown-type -ENODEV likewise (532-535). The old precondition that clocks and reset GPIO were already acquired by the caller was wrong: the function acquires them (482-495) and can fail there. Also the supply-enable failure path skips the bulk disable (err_dcvdd). madera_dev_init at 454-764; read fully.

name: altera_execute
prose: Precondition: astate points to a valid initialised altera_state (config, msg_buff and stack usable), p points to program_size readable bytes holding a JAM/STAPL byte-code image, and error_address, exit_code and format_version point to writable ints. Postcondition: this is altera_execute, the JAM interpreter. If program_size > 52 it reads the header, sets *format_version to version + 1 (1 or 2) and reads the table offsets and counts; if the first word is not 0x4A414D00 or 0x4A414D01 (this includes program_size <= 52) it returns -EIO without executing. If the symbol count is 0 it skips the variable setup and continues with no variables. Otherwise it allocates the variable, size and attribute arrays (and the procedure attribute array for version > 0), returning -ENOMEM through the common exit if any allocation fails, and initialises every symbol (scalars, compressed Boolean arrays decompressed into newly allocated buffers with -EIO on a decompression failure or -ENOMEM, uninitialised arrays zero-allocated). It then initialises the interpreter and, for format version 2, requires aconf->action (-EINVAL if it is NULL or names no action in the image), finds the first procedure to run (a computed program counter outside the code section gives -ERANGE) or finishes at once if no procedure is to be executed. It then runs the byte code until done: each opcode is decoded and executed; an unrecognised opcode gives -ENOSYS, a stack underflow (altera_check_stack) or a stack pointer outside the stack gives -EOVERFLOW, and many individual opcodes give -ERANGE for invalid variable types, counts or branch targets, or another negative errno from a helper, but not every array index is bounds-checked (for example OP_POPE stores into the array at the popped index without checking it against the array size). OP_RET with an empty stack at version 1 or later sets *exit_code to 0 when no procedure remains; other opcodes can set *exit_code from the stack. When a non-zero status ends execution inside the loop, *error_address is set to the offset of the failing opcode from the start of the code section (it is not set for failures before the loop). It always frees the interpreter buffers, the dynamically allocated arrays (those with attribute bit 7) and the variable, size, attribute and procedure arrays before returning, takes no locks, and returns 0 on completion or the negative status above.
note: Reviewer 3 right: OP_POPE (altera.c:1081-1141) writes longptr_tmp[index] with an index popped from the stack and not checked against var_size, so the old claim 'ERANGE for an invalid index' was too broad. Also corrected: stack under/overflow is -EOVERFLOW (altera_check_stack at 120-127 and 2066-2067), not -ERANGE, and an unrecognised opcode is -ENOSYS (2063-2064); neither was in the old prose. altera_execute is 204-2088: a ~1900-line interpreter with 72 opcode cases of which I read the header/setup, OP_RET, OP_POPE, the last comparison opcode and the loop epilogue, and grepped every status assignment; I did NOT read every opcode, so the prose states the cross-cutting behaviour only. Large function read partly.

name: altera_execute
prose: Precondition: astate points to a valid initialised altera_state (config, msg_buff and stack usable), p points to program_size readable bytes holding a JAM/STAPL byte-code image, and error_address, exit_code and format_version point to writable ints. note: This item (altera.c:261-513, the unnamed setup slice) is the header/setup part of the same function altera_execute (204-2088), so it is described under its real name with the same text as the other altera_execute item. The old prose for this slot was already about the right function. Large function read partly (see the other item).

name: bcm_vk_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a valid, unbound pci_dev, ent its matching id; the module parameters nr_ib_sgl_blk, nr_scratch_pages and auto_load are readable (nr_ib_sgl_blk is clamped to BCM_VK_IB_SGL_BLK_MAX). Postcondition: this is bcm_vk_probe. kzalloc failure returns -ENOMEM directly. pci_enable_device failure frees vk and returns the error (the only unwind on that path). On success of that call it takes a reference with pci_dev_get and then: pci_request_regions, dma_set_mask_and_coherent, an optional coherent scratch buffer, pci_set_master and drvdata, pci_alloc_irq_vectors (a count below VK_MSIX_IRQ_MIN_REQ returns -EINVAL, or the negative error returned), pci_ioremap_bar for each BAR (-ENOMEM on failure), devm_request_irq for the message-queue, notification and tty interrupts, ida_alloc, kstrdup of the device name (-ENOMEM), misc_register, a single-thread workqueue (-ENOMEM), bcm_vk_msg_init, the panic notifier registration, bcm_vk_tty_init and, if auto_load is set and the boot ROM is running, bcm_vk_trigger_autoload (if auto_load is set but the ROM is not running it only logs), and finally bcm_vk_hb_init; it returns 0 and leaves vk owned by the driver. A failure unwinds through labels in reverse order, each undoing what was acquired before the failing step: tty exit, notifier unregister, workqueue destroy, misc deregister, name free, ida_free, then (err_irq) devm_free_irq of the requested vectors plus pci_disable_msix and pci_disable_msi, then (err_iounmap) iounmap of the mapped BARs and pci_release_regions, then (err_disable_pdev) free of the scratch buffer if allocated, pci_free_irq_vectors, pci_disable_device and pci_dev_put, and finally kfree(vk). Failures of pci_request_regions, dma_set_mask_and_coherent, the scratch allocation and pci_alloc_irq_vectors jump to err_disable_pdev, so they do not call pci_release_regions even when the regions were already requested (all except the request_regions failure itself) and do not unmap BARs. Errors are returned as the failing call's value or the -ENOMEM/-EINVAL values given above.
note: Reviewer 1 mostly wrong: the irq-vector shortfall jumps to err_disable_pdev (bcm_vk_dev.c:1350), which calls pci_free_irq_vectors (1524), so the vectors are freed; reviewer 3 mixed: both pci_free_irq_vectors (at err_disable_pdev) and pci_disable_msix/pci_disable_msi (at err_irq, 1509-1510) exist, on different paths; reviewer 2 right (pci_enable_device failure only kfrees vk). Extra finding: failures at the DMA mask, scratch-buffer and IRQ-vector steps skip pci_release_regions although pci_request_regions already succeeded (they go to err_disable_pdev, not err_iounmap). bcm_vk_probe at 1279-1532. I did not read the callees.

name: bcm_vk_read
prose: Precondition: p_file->private_data is a valid bcm_vk_ctx of a bcm_vk device and buf is a user buffer; because the too-small-buffer path copies one block of VK_MSGQ_BLK_SIZE bytes regardless of count, buf should be writable for at least VK_MSGQ_BLK_SIZE bytes even when count is smaller. Postcondition: it returns -EPERM without touching any queue if bcm_vk_drv_access_ok(vk) fails. Otherwise, holding chan->pendq_lock with spin_lock and releasing it before any user copy, it scans the to-host pending queues in index order (highest priority first) for the first entry whose ctx->idx equals the caller's ctx->idx and handles only that entry. If no entry matches it returns -ENOMSG. If the entry matches and count is at least to_h_blks * VK_MSGQ_BLK_SIZE, it unlinks it from the pending queue and decrements ctx->pend_cnt, then outside the lock restores the user message id in the first block, copies to_h_blks * VK_MSGQ_BLK_SIZE bytes to buf, frees the entry with bcm_vk_free_wkent whether or not the copy worked, and returns the byte count on success or -ENOMSG if copy_to_user fails (the message is then lost). If the entry matches but count is smaller, the entry stays queued with pend_cnt unchanged, and it copies the first block, with the user message id and the size field set to to_h_blks - 1, to buf (always VK_MSGQ_BLK_SIZE bytes) and returns -EMSGSIZE, or -EFAULT if that copy fails.
note: Reviewer right: the -EMSGSIZE path copies a full first block (VK_MSGQ_BLK_SIZE) with copy_to_user even if count is smaller (bcm_vk_msg.c:1069), so the old precondition (buf of at least count bytes) understated what must be writable. Rest of the old prose matched the code. Slice cut the head: function is bcm_vk_read at 1003-1075 (the name was right).

name: fastrpc_init
prose: Precondition: module-init context; neither fastrpc_cb_driver nor fastrpc_driver is registered. Postcondition: it registers the callback platform driver fastrpc_cb_driver with platform_driver_register; if that returns a negative value it logs an error and returns that value, with neither driver registered. Otherwise it registers the rpmsg driver fastrpc_driver with register_rpmsg_driver; if that returns a negative value it logs an error, unregisters the platform driver again with platform_driver_unregister and returns that negative value (the rpmsg driver is not registered). If both succeed it returns 0 with both drivers registered. It takes no locks itself.
note: Prose matched fastrpc_init (fastrpc.c:2537-2555). Reviewers' points concerned the old formal contract only (too weak), which I removed (rule 4: the function registers global drivers, so a pure contract does not apply). Slice cut the head; read fully.

name: lis3_i2c_blockread
prose: Precondition: lis3->bus_priv points to a valid i2c_client, reg is a register number, len is non-negative and v points to a writable buffer large enough for the number of bytes that will be read (at most I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX, 32, because i2c_smbus_read_i2c_block_data limits the length to that). Postcondition: it sets bit 7 of the register number in its own local copy (auto-increment addressing; the caller's variable is unchanged) and returns the value of i2c_smbus_read_i2c_block_data(c, reg, len, v): the number of bytes read into v (normally the length clamped to 32, but any count returned by that function, possibly fewer than requested) or a negative errno on failure. It takes no locks itself and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewers 2 and 3 right: len above 32 is clamped and the returned count can be smaller than len; the function just forwards the return value of i2c_smbus_read_i2c_block_data (lis3lv02d_i2c.c:59-65). Reviewer 1 right (positive byte count on success). Static inline; slice cut the head.

name: mei_cl_dma_alloc_and_map
prose: Precondition: the caller holds dev->device_lock, cl is non-NULL with cl->dev set, dev->hbm_f_cd_supported is true, buffer_id is nonzero, cl is not connected, cl->dma_mapped is false, and no client dma with buffer_id is already allocated. Postcondition: it returns 0 (after the same pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and control cb release as on the failure paths) only when the wait ended with cl->status == 0 (the dma is mapped and the allocation is kept), and otherwise a negative errno: -ENODEV when cl or cl->dev is invalid or the HBM dma map request cannot be sent, -EOPNOTSUPP when client dma is unsupported, -EINVAL when buffer_id is 0, -EPROTO when the client is connected, already dma_mapped, or buffer_id is already allocated, the error from pm_runtime_get when it is negative and not -EINPROGRESS, the error from mei_cl_dma_alloc, -ENOMEM when the control cb cannot be allocated, -EFAULT when the wait times out (including when the hbuf could not be acquired so no request was sent), or the cl->status value set by the completion; on every nonzero return after mei_cl_dma_alloc succeeded the dma allocation is released with mei_cl_dma_free, the control cb is freed with mei_io_cb_free (NULL-safe), dev->device_lock is dropped around the wait and reacquired before returning, and the pm_runtime reference taken by pm_runtime_get is balanced by pm_runtime_put_autosuspend (or by pm_runtime_put_noidle on the pm_runtime_get and mei_cl_dma_alloc failure paths).
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: the function is mei_cl_dma_alloc_and_map(cl, fp, buffer_id, size) (mei/client.c:2297-2358); there is no mei_cl_dma_map. I checked every return and the out label against the old prose, which was correct, and only added that the pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and cb release also happen on success. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: mei_dma_ring_write
prose: Precondition: dev is a valid mei_device whose DMA ring control block exists and whose host buffer size gives a non-zero power-of-two depth in 32-bit slots; the caller has ensured the ring has room for mei_data2slots(len) slots (no free-space check is done); buf points to at least mei_data2slots(len) * 4 readable bytes, i.e. len rounded up to a multiple of 4, because the copy reads whole slots. Postcondition: if the control block pointer is NULL it raises WARN_ON and returns without touching the ring. Otherwise it computes the write slot index as hbuf_wr_idx & (hbuf_depth - 1) and the number of slots as mei_data2slots(len); if the slots would pass the end of the host buffer it copies the part up to the end of the buffer, then continues with the remaining slots from index 0; it copies with memcpy in units of 4 bytes per slot, and finally advances ctrl->hbuf_wr_idx by the slot count with WRITE_ONCE (the index is not reduced modulo the depth here). It returns nothing and takes no locks.
note: Reviewer right: mei_dma_copy_to (dma-ring.c:152-163) copies n << 2 bytes per call, so up to three bytes beyond len are read from buf when len is not a multiple of 4; the old precondition (len readable bytes) was too weak. Slice cut the head; mei_dma_ring_write at 248-273.

name: hdr_is_valid
prose: Precondition: none; msg_hdr may be any 32-bit value, read through the struct mei_msg_hdr bitfield layout (little-endian: length in bits 16-24, reserved in bits 25-27, extended in bit 28, dma_ring in bit 29). Postcondition: it returns 0 exactly when msg_hdr is nonzero, its reserved field is zero, and its length field is at least 4 (MEI_SLOT_SIZE) times the number of set flags among dma_ring and extended; in every other case it returns -EBADMSG (-74); it has no side effects.
note: Verified against interrupt.c:331-348 and the bit layout in hw.h:411-421 (me_addr 0-7, host_addr 8-15, length 16-24, reserved 25-27, extended 28, dma_ring 29; MEI_SLOT_SIZE = sizeof(u32) = 4): the checks are msg_hdr zero or reserved non-zero, then length below 4 per set flag among dma_ring and extended, each giving -EBADMSG (-74), else 0. Prose and contract unchanged; the earlier 'still-rejected' complaints were mechanical (older contract omitted -74).

name: mei_ioctl
prose: Precondition: file->private_data is a mei_cl with a non-NULL dev, data is a user pointer appropriate for cmd, and the caller does not hold dev->device_lock (the function takes it). Postcondition: if cl or cl->dev is NULL it warns and returns -ENODEV before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes dev->device_lock and returns -ENODEV (after releasing it) if dev->dev_state is not MEI_DEV_ENABLED. For IOCTL_MEI_CONNECT_CLIENT it copies the connect data from user (-EFAULT on failure) and calls mei_vt_support_check: a result of -ENOTTY is returned; a result of 0 connects with mei_ioctl_connect_vtag using vtag 0; any other non-zero result (for example -EOPNOTSUPP) connects with mei_ioctl_connect_client; a non-zero connect result is returned, otherwise the connect data is copied back to user, returning -EFAULT if that copy fails (the connection having already been made). For IOCTL_MEI_CONNECT_CLIENT_VTAG it copies the vtag connect data from user (-EFAULT), returns any non-zero mei_vt_support_check result (with a debug message for -EOPNOTSUPP), returns -EINVAL for a zero vtag, calls mei_ioctl_connect_vtag (its error returned) and copies the data back (-EFAULT on failure). For IOCTL_MEI_NOTIFY_SET it copies a u32 from user (-EFAULT) and returns the result of mei_ioctl_client_notify_request (nothing is copied back). For IOCTL_MEI_NOTIFY_GET it calls mei_ioctl_client_notify_get (error returned) and copies the u32 result to user (-EFAULT on failure). Any other cmd returns -ENOIOCTLCMD. On every return after the lock was taken it releases dev->device_lock before returning; it returns 0 on success.
note: Reviewer 1 (old precondition said the caller holds the lock) and reviewer 3 (the early -ENODEV return is before mutex_lock, mei/main.c:679-680, so the lock was never taken) both right, and reflected: the old text said the lock was released on every return path. Extra: for IOCTL_MEI_CONNECT_CLIENT only -ENOTTY from mei_vt_support_check aborts; other non-zero values select the non-vtag connect (704-711). mei_ioctl at 666-798.

name: mei_me_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a PCI device bound to this driver and ent is the matching pci_device_id whose driver_data selects a mei_cfg. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV if mei_me_get_cfg finds no config or if mei_me_quirk_probe rejects the device. Otherwise it enables the device with pcim_enable_device, sets bus mastering, maps BAR 0 with pcim_iomap_regions and sets a 64-bit DMA mask (each error is returned after logging; these steps use devres so there is nothing else to undo), allocates and initialises the MEI device with mei_me_dev_init (-ENOMEM if it returns NULL), registers it with mei_register (its error returned, with only devres resources to release), tries pci_enable_msi (the result is ignored), and requests the threaded IRQ with request_threaded_irq. If that call fails it goes to the deregister exit with the request_threaded_irq error; that exit cancels MEI work, disables interrupts, calls free_irq on pdev->irq with dev (even though the request failed, so no IRQ was installed by this function) and calls mei_deregister. Then mei_start is called; if it fails the function returns -ENODEV through the same deregister exit (which frees the IRQ that was installed). On success it configures runtime PM autosuspend, stores dev as pdev's driver data, sets DPM_FLAG_NO_DIRECT_COMPLETE and the MEI PM domain, and, if power gating is enabled, drops the runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_put_noidle and, if d0i3_supported, allows runtime PM; it returns 0 with the device registered and the IRQ installed. Every failure logs 'initialization failed'; the caller gets no ownership of dev or the IRQ.
note: Reviewer 1 right (mei_start failure returns -ENODEV, pci-me.c:250-253); reviewer 2 wrong (mei_start failure goes to the deregister label, which does call free_irq, 291); reviewer 3 right in effect: a request_threaded_irq failure also goes to deregister (244-247) and so free_irq is called although no IRQ was installed. Old prose said both failures 'free the IRQ' without saying one of them frees an IRQ that was never requested. mei_me_probe at 183-296.

name: vsc_get_sensor_name
prose: Precondition: fw_loader is an initialised vsc_fw_loader whose sensor_name is a character array (assumed to end in a NUL byte, since this function copies only the string bytes and does not write a terminator), and dev is a valid device. Postcondition: this is vsc_get_sensor_name. It returns -EINVAL if ACPI_HANDLE(dev) is NULL. Otherwise it evaluates the ACPI method SID with one integer argument (1) into an automatically allocated buffer; if the evaluation fails it logs and returns -ENODEV, and if the returned buffer pointer is NULL it logs and returns -ENODEV (in these two cases it does not call ACPI_FREE). If the returned object is not a string it returns -ENODEV, and if the string length is not smaller than sizeof(fw_loader->sensor_name) it returns -EINVAL; on these two paths sensor_name is not modified. Otherwise it copies the string bytes into fw_loader->sensor_name with memcpy (no terminating NUL is written) and lower-cases the buffer in place with string_lower, then returns 0. On every path that obtained a buffer pointer (the non-string, too-long and success paths) it frees the ACPI buffer with ACPI_FREE and keeps no reference to it.
note: Not a drop: the slice 267-517 starts inside vsc_get_sensor_name (vsc-fw-loader.c:249-304); the old prose described the right function but said the ACPI buffer was freed on every path after the handle check, which is wrong for the evaluation-failure and NULL-pointer returns (they return without ACPI_FREE, 275-285), and it assumed a terminator that the code does not write (292-298).

name: gru_intr
prose: Precondition: chiplet and blade identify a valid GRU chiplet (indices into gru_base[blade]->bs_grus[]) whose TLB-miss interrupt is being serviced, and the caller holds no locks. Postcondition: the function reads and clears the chiplet's instruction- and data-fault maps, completes the blade's async completion (bs_async_wq) once for each CBR whose done bit is set if that completion pointer is non-NULL, and for each instruction-fault bit fetches the TFH, looks up the thread state for the TFH's context number, skips the entry (counting a spurious interrupt) when no thread state is registered, and otherwise counts an FMM TLB miss and puts the TFH into user polling mode; it then returns IRQ_HANDLED, taking no locks and keeping no references (the IRQ_NONE return for a missing GRU is unreachable because gru is the address of an array element and can never be NULL).
note: Checked line by line against grufault.c:452-510. Reviewer 2 right and already reflected in the prose (the !gru test at 464 is dead since gru is the address of an array element). Reviewer 3 wrong for this version of the code: gru_intr has no gru_try_dropin call; each instruction-fault bit just counts fmm_tlbmiss and switches the TFH to user polling mode (505-507). Reviewer 1 concerned the old contract only. Prose unchanged. Slice cut the head.
